name: open-in-chat

frames.best_why: Frame 2 opens the dropdown of all five AI destinations with icons and external-link marks.

tagline: Buttons and a dropdown that send a prompt into ChatGPT, Claude or Perplexity.
summary: A small control that turns a prompt into links opening it in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Grok or v0. It can appear as an inline row of brand icons or as a dropdown under one trigger.
appearance: A card footer with a pale bar holding the label Ask AI and five tiny brand marks, plus an outlined Open in chat button with a chevron. The open menu is a dark rounded panel of five labelled rows, each with a brand glyph and a small external-link arrow.
behaviour: Clicking the trigger drops the list of assistants; choosing a row opens that service in a new tab with the prompt filled into its query. The inline version shows each site as an icon, and hovering one shows a tooltip naming it.
demo_content: A guide card titled Optimistic updates with a prompt about optimistic updates in a React form.
search_phrases: ask ai links for an article
pass a prompt to another ai
share question with an ai tool
hand off text to a chatbot
use_when: A docs or blog page wants readers to continue a question in a full AI chat instead of a short callout.
avoid_when: It only opens external sites with a query string; it does no streaming, history or answer rendering itself.
customise: Pass the prompt and pick the dropdown or horizontal layout; override the trigger label and alignment, or render custom OpenInChatLink children to change the destinations.
weight_why: A trigger with a Radix menu of five links and no fetching or animation loop.

a11y.note: Keyboard and labels are solid; the menu's entrance animation has no reduced-motion guard.

issues: The five inline icons are tiny and all the same grey, so they are hard to tell apart.
Showing both a dropdown and an icon row in one footer makes it feel redundant.
polish_why: Tidy, well-labelled links with a clear menu; the tiny duplicate icon row is the weak part.
